definition: The relationship between grid-wide generation/consumption balance and the AC system's oscillation frequency, and the corrective actions taken when frequency drifts.
core_idea: System frequency depends on generation staying balanced with consumption; when frequency drops too low the grid must increase production or cut consumption, and when it rises too high generators must decrease production or consumption must increase — which is why ancillary services are framed around frequency maintenance.
key_points: Frequency is the number of oscillations per second on the AC grid.
Low frequency signals a need to increase production or reduce consumption.
High frequency signals a need to decrease production or increase consumption.
Ancillary services are commonly discussed in terms of their role in maintaining system frequency.
relationships: Explains the purpose of regulation up/down and reserve ancillary services.
